Confessions of a Convert

by

Robert Hugh Benson

LONGMANS, GREEN, AND CO.

FOURTH AVENUE & 30TH STREET, NEW YORK

LONDON, BOMBAY, AND CALCUTTA

1913

Preface
 
The following chapters were 
first published, in substance, in the American Catholic Magazine, The 
"Ave Maria," in 1906-1907 . . .

Chapter One
 
When one stands at last 
upon high ground, it is extraordinarily difficult to trace the road 
behind . . .

Chapter Two
 
Up to the time of my 
father's death I do not think that a doubt had ever crossed my mind as 
to the claims of Catholicism.

Chapter Three
 
It will be impossible 
for me ever to acknowledge adequately the debt of gratitude which I owe 
to the Community of the Resurrection . . .

Chapter Four
 
I think that it was in 
the summer and autumn of 1902 that I began to write a book called "The 
Light Invisible."

Chapter Five
 
Gradually, however, 
three things drew out of the clamouring mob of ideas and 
authors.

Chapter Six
 
I was in a very curious 
and unsatisfactory state when I came home.

Chapter Seven
 
I do not suppose that 
anyone ever entered the City of God with less emotion than mine.

Chapter Eight
 
And now I do not know 
whether it is respectful to my holy mother the Church to attempt to say 
what she has been to me ever since the day that I walked blind and dumb 
and miserable into her arms.

Dedicated to

FATHER REGINALD BUCKLER, O.P.

whose hand unlocked for me the gate of the

City of God and led me in
